howToFill: Copy this file to va2_voices.json in the work folder and fill it on the machine that runs the engines.

Start AivisSpeech and the VOICEVOX Nemo engine, then run: python va2_render.py voices --voices va2_voices.json --out <work>. It lists every installed speaker and style with its id (also saved as speakers_aivis.json and speakers_nemo.json) and says what is still missing here.

styles: the style ids of ONE speaker of ONE model. 'normal' is its neutral style (ノーマル / 通常 / Normal); 'upbeat' its brightest (テンション高め, 上機嫌, 喜び, 元気…) or null if it has none; 'calm' (落ち着き, 穏やか…) or null.

licence: the model's licence as its AivisHub page or AIVM metadata states it (for example ACML 1.0, CC0, a custom licence), and whether it allows use in a free, distributed game with credit. A model whose terms do not allow that is not used.
why: one line on why this voice fits the slot. Nobody has heard these: say 'not yet heard' until Robin has.

AV-girl.want: an energetic young girl (a child), bright and bouncy

AV-bright.want: a bright, bubbly young woman (a cheerful shopkeeper or helper)

AV-sweet.want: a sweet, gentle but energetic young woman (not breathy)

AV-showy.want: a high-energy performer or announcer woman

AV-suzu-A.want: Suzu, the travelling performer (set 3, voice A): a projecting, energetic stage voice; a model distinct from the narrators and the other slots

AV-suzu-B.want: Suzu, the travelling performer (set 3, voice B): a warmer, huskier, witty voice; a model distinct from AV-suzu-A

cat_meow.want: one basic, clean domestic cat meow (about 0.5–1.5 s) for Mochi; CC0 or public domain only, confirmed on the recording's own page

NM-A.want: the Nemo voice Robin preferred in VA-1 for the middle-aged man (npc08): warm, ordinary

NM-B.want: another Nemo male voice, gruffer and lower

NM-C.want: another Nemo male voice, brisker and lighter (a clerk)
